answers.question: Trains AI models on customer data
answers.value: No under Privacy Policy/Security page unless explicitly agreed in writing; HOWEVER 1 Aug 2026 Client Terms authorise use of User Content to train foundation models with Client consent. Material policy/contract discrepancy.
answers.note: Client Terms effective 1 Aug 2026 include authorisation for use of User Content to train base foundation models; Privacy Policy says not used to train public third-party models.

answers.question: How long prompts and chats are kept
answers.value: Retention not specified as a single fixed duration; platform retention per privacy/DPA and customer settings
answers.note: Subprocessor list includes OpenAI, Serper, Laminar, HeyGen, ElevenLabs, etc. Laminar receives prompts and outputs for tracing/evaluation.

answers.note: DPA says AI-assisted authoring, assessment and grading are designed for human review before content is published/results released.

answers.value: Set by the educator; gives answers directly (AI Tutor)

answers.question: Answers from your own course content
answers.note: Terms describe RAG indexing authorised content to generate course material.

answers.question: Who owns what the AI produces
answers.value: Client/User retains AI output IP subject to law and human-authorship rules; Client Terms preserve broad rights and consent language.
answers.note: Client Terms allocate rights but also authorise processing/training under stated consent. Privacy and contract clauses need reconciliation.

researchTasks: [Critical] Conflict between privacy/security assurances and Client Terms re foundation-model training: Please reconcile the 1 Aug 2026 Client Terms clause authorising use of User Content to train base foundation models with the 8 Sep 2026 Privacy Policy and Security page stating no training unless explicitly agreed. Which term controls? Can you provide a signed opt-out/no-training clause? (route: privacy@coursebox.ai / account manager; evidence wanted: Signed DPA, current Client Terms, AI data-flow diagram, training opt-out clause)
Reconcile differences between current privacy/DPA and client-terms language on model training and output ownership; verify whether all plan tiers share identical controls.

Ask vendor (Trains AI models on customer data): Please reconcile the 1 Aug 2026 Client Terms clause authorising foundation-model training with the Privacy Policy/Security page stating no training unless expressly agreed. Which term prevails for enterprise clients?
Ask vendor (Staff can see learner conversations): Can staff set limits, review learner chats and approve grading before release? Please provide feature-level controls.
Ask vendor (How it responds to learners): Is the AI designed to coach learners with questions/hints, follow educator-defined behaviour, or provide direct answers? Can this be configured?
Ask vendor (Shows its sources): Can AI Tutor be configured to answer exclusively from a defined course/tenant knowledge base, and are citations shown?
Researcher note (learnerOversight), not shown until sourced: Age value is a minimum eligibility signal only; check school/parent consent and local jurisdictional requirements.

Researcher note (outputOwnership), not shown until sourced: Client Terms dated 1 Aug 2026 state client authorises use of User Content to train base foundation models unless otherwise constrained by agreement; Privacy Policy dated 8 Sep 2026 and Security page say no training unless explicitly agreed in writing. Obtain written contractual clarification.
